Check which parameters a dataset can inform, before fitting

Source: R/ctIdentify.R
ctIdentify.Rd

Reports the directions of the parameter space the data carry no information about, and the parameters involved in them, without fitting the model.

Usage

ctIdentify(
  datalong,
  model,
  inits = NULL,
  nstart = 3L,
  spread = 0.5,
  priors = FALSE,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  verbose = 0L,
  rtol = 1e-13,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

datalong

Long format data, as for ctFit.

model

Model from ctModel.

inits

Optional evaluation point. Supplying one uses that single point, without the comparison across points described in Details.

nstart

Number of points to evaluate. The first is the origin of the unconstrained space, and the rest are dispersed draws around it.

spread

Standard deviation of the additional evaluation points on the raw scale.

priors

Whether to include the prior. FALSE by default, because a prior informs every direction, so a model the data do not identify looks fine with priors on.

cores

As for ctFit.

verbose

As for ctFit.

rtol

A direction counts as uninformed when the information along it is below this fraction of the best informed direction's. The default separates zero from small, so that only structurally unidentified directions are reported. Raise it to report weakly identified directions too, including some a fit would settle.

seed

Seed for the dispersed evaluation points, so that identical calls give identical output. The session's random stream is restored afterwards. NULL draws from the session's stream instead.

...

Further arguments to ctFit that shape the model, such as intoverpop or poprank, with ctFit's defaults.

Value

An object of class ctIdentify, with $parameters (names in the flat directions at every evaluation point), $partial and $structural (those split into the partially and completely unidentified), $sometimes (in a flat direction at some points only), $rotating (whether the flat directions change between points), $nweak, $condition, $starts (the detail for each point), and $effects, the information about the random effects at a supplied inits (NULL otherwise). Printing it summarises what was found.

Details

This finds structural non-identification, such as parameters that only appear together, a latent process nothing measures, or a scale that is never fixed. These are properties of the model that hold wherever it is evaluated. A direction can be flat at one point and well informed at the estimate, so several points are used, and only parameters in the flat directions at every point are reported as uninformed.

The model is prepared by ctFit, with any of its arguments given in ..., so what is checked is the model a fit with the same arguments would estimate.

A random effect on a variance parameter (DIFFUSION, MANIFESTVAR) under intoverpop = 'augmented' with a full rank population covariance (poprank = NA) is partially identified. The population covariances it implies with the other varying parameters are determined, but their split into a scale and correlations is not. The printed summary separates partial from complete non-identification, because the advice differs: fixing a value discards information in the first case, and is the fix in the second.

Requires the julia backend, which supplies the per-subject scores. The information has rank at most the number of subjects, so a model with more free parameters than subjects shows flat directions for that reason alone, and the printed summary says when that applies.

How well the data determine each random effect's population standard deviation, and how much of each subject's effect its own data determine, is checked only at a supplied inits, such as a fit's estimate$raw. ctFit makes the same check at its estimate, stored as fit$identifiability$effects. It depends on the population standard deviations, so at the default evaluation points it would describe the starting values instead of the data.

See also

ctFit runs the equivalent check on a finished fit, evaluated at the estimate and stored as fit$identifiability.

Examples

# \donttest{
# ctIdentify() always uses the julia backend internally, whatever the
# eventual fit will use, so the example is inert where Julia is absent --
# including on CRAN, whose check machines have none.
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
  gen <- suppressMessages(ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = 1,
    manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1', LAMBDA = matrix(1),
    DRIFT = matrix(-0.4), DIFFUSION = matrix(0.6), MANIFESTVAR = matrix(0.3),
    T0VAR = matrix(1), T0MEANS = matrix(0), CINT = matrix(0),
    MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(0), Tpoints = 8))
  datalong <- ctGenerate(gen, n = 40, Tpoints = 8, backend = 'r')

  model <- suppressMessages(ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = 1,
    manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1', LAMBDA = matrix(1),
    T0MEANS = matrix(0), CINT = matrix(0), MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(0)))

  result <- ctIdentify(datalong, model, cores = 1)
  print(result)
  # Julia keeps running between calls, holding what it has compiled;
  # this ends it.
  ctJuliaKill("session")
}
# }
